newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka central bank sees a BOP surplus in 1997. [CORRECTED 11:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka central bank sees a BOP surplus in 1997. [CORRECTED 11:40 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects to make clear that the bank sees a balance of payments surplus, not a trade surplus.)
Sri Lanka expects to see an overall balance of payments (BoP) surplus for 1997 after two years of deficit, the Central Bank governor said on Friday.
"We expect to see an overall BoP surplus this year," Amarananda Jayawardena told Reuters in an interview on Friday.
"The surplus should be around 180 million SDRs this year," Jayawardene said, adding that last year Sri Lanka had a BoP deficit of 62 million SDR.
"The surplus will be largely driven by privatisation proceeds and moderate capital inflows," he added.
The government aims to raise five billion rupees ($85.6 million) by privatising several state firms this year.
Jayawardena forecast that exports and imports should both grow by 13 percent in 1997.
The trade deficit in the first four months was $534 million, an increase of 8.3 percent over the same period last year.
"Imports are generally higher in April," Jayawardena said. Last year exports grew by 13 percent and imports by seven percent, the Central Bank has said.
